notes: Q2 FY2026 print is the review-gate quarter (PF_STRAT.REVIEW_GATES). Headline beat is real and broad: AWS +37% YoY (fastest in 18 quarters, vs 31% consensus) blows through the OLD bull-case KPI ceiling (32%); ad growth +26% also clears the old bull threshold; consolidated op margin hit a new record 13.7% even while absorbing a raised capex guide. But the thesis's own bull condition has two legs, and they diverged this quarter: AWS re-acceleration confirmed hard, while FCF (TTM) got WORSE, not better (-$7.6B vs +$18.2B a year ago), and full-year capex guide was raised again to $220B from $200B (cited: higher memory costs + AI/cloud infra). This is the exact pull-forward/monetization tension CLAUDE.md flags: capacity selling out explains the capex, but only AWS revenue+margin, not just growth, justifies it — and margin did hold, so this reads as a genuine monetization data point, not just a threat-justified spend. GAAP net income ($62.6B, EPS $5.75) is heavily inflated by a $53.4B pretax Anthropic mark-to-market gain (non-operating) — clean/operating comparison should use the $27.5B op income (+43% YoY) instead. FTC ad-suit still unresolved (prepared but not filed as of late June 2026; broader 2023 monopoly case trial slated Oct 2026) — narrative unchanged, still a live pending risk, not yet a realized one.
